title: Police 'did their duty' in fatal shooting, SIU says
article: The provincial Special Investigations Unit has cleared a Toronto Police officer in the fatal shooting of a man who stabbed his sister and niece at a North York home.
The SIU said the shooting of 34-year-old Ucal Lauzon, who died of a gunshot wound to the torso, was legally justified.
Lauzon was shot after he stabbed his 62-year-old sister, Pandora Whyte, and 37-year-old niece Marcia Whyte. Marcia has recovered from her injuries. Pandora died at the scene.

The SIU said Lauzon came to Pandora's townhouse at 1898 Sheppard Ave. W. near Jane Street around 6 p.m. May 27. Pandora's 15-year- old daughter was also there. Pandora asked Lauzon to leave because of past problems, but he refused. She then called another daughter, Marcia, and told her of Lauzon's unwanted presence.

Marcia called police at 11:02 p.m. to report that she was on her way to the townhouse and asked police to go there as well. She told police her uncle was mentally unstable and had been violent in the past.
Meanwhile, Lauzon fatally stabbed Pandora in her living room and tried to hurt the 15-year-old. The teen managed to escape and call police.
Marcia then entered the home and was stabbed numerous times by Lauzon. She escaped through a side door and collapsed on the sidewalk.

Police officers arrived at 11:05 p.m., entered the home and saw Lauzon standing near Pandora with a knife. The officers drew their firearms and ordered Lauzon to drop the knife. When Lauzon turned toward an officer who had entered through the front door, an officer fired twice.
Lauzon was taken to hospital where he died.

"The threat of lethal force was met with lethal force," said SIU director James Cornish in a news release. "The involved officers had ample reason to believe that Mr. Lauzon was a dangerous person and that he had just gravely wounded two people. They were duty bound to enter into an inherently dangerous situation and they did their duty. When they entered, the officers all saw that Mr. Lauzon had a knife and they all perceived his last motions to be the commencement of an attack."
The SIU, which investigates whenever there is a serious injury, sexual assault or death involving police, had assigned eight investigators to the case.
The civilian agency had designated one subject and seven witness officers.
